newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends off on profit taking, cash gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends off on profit taking, cash gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures, hit by profit taking after last week's rally, ended lower Monday in moderate trade, but firmer cash prices left many expecting only limited downside near-term.
June skidded 4.7 cents to close at $2.22 per million British thermal units. July settled 3.2 cents lower at $2.257. Others ended down by 1.8 to 5.8 cents.
"The market took a breather today, but I think we'll see more upside. Cash still looks pretty good," said one East Coast trader, noting cash seemed well-bid this month.

Technical traders agreed the market was overbought and due for a correction after a nine percent rally last week, but most saw only limited downside near-term, with cash firm and better cooling loads just around the corner.
"I don't expect a big selloff. There are (cash) buyers lining up at lower numbers," said an eastern cash trader, adding a move above $2.30 (in June) could be a struggle.
Chart traders pegged resistance in June at $2.33 and then at the $2.385 contract high. Support was seen at $2.17, then at $2.05 and along the up trendline at $2.03.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed a couple of cents Monday to near the $2.20 level. Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly at about $2. New York city gate gas was slightly firmer in the mid-to-high $2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Hub strip fell 2.7 cents to $2.302. NYMEX said 35,133 contracts traded, down from Friday's revised tally of 39,389.

On the KCBT, June finished 3.7 cents lower at $2.06, while deferreds ended steady to down 2.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by one cent to 16.0 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 405 lots changed hands, up slightly from Friday's total of 397.
